evidence: (a) Equivalent semantics are present: the receipts subtree goal applies to 'Every pending ACK-required message'; the root explicitly preserves terminal states and says 'Late ACK clears the existing warning through normal lifecycle'. Invitations state 'Only explicit recipient acceptance settles it automatically', without a before-deadline condition, and the subtree says timed invitations 'settle at acceptance'. Thus confirmation ends a pending obligation; due scanning discovers outstanding work, rather than necessarily synthesizing a historical warning after settlement. (b) The stated goal is a bounded-time warning 'when receipt or explicitly requested invitation acceptance is unconfirmed', and the root expressly uses the 'normal bounded scan'. 'An overdue warning says confirmation missed its deadline' constrains a warning's meaning; it does not require a warning for every historical miss after confirmation has already settled the obligation. (c) Requiring an atomic late-confirmation transition that always records a missed-deadline warning adds a deadline-audit guarantee absent from this scope. (d) The proposed race has already obtained the requested receipt/acceptance before warning discovery, so the sender no longer needs the recovery attention that this design promises. A boundary test could clarify implementation expectations, but the claimed mandatory historical warning rule is not a material missing requirement.
